# Snippets

Rendered with `{% render 'name', param: value %}`. Parameters come from each snippet's LiquidDoc header.

## ai-label

File: `snippets/ai-label.liquid`

A small "AI" label for the bottom right corner of an image, shown when the
image's own alt text says it is AI made: the lowercased alt contains
"ai generated" or "ai altered" (a hyphen counts as a space, so "AI-generated"
matches too). Merchants control it by writing that in the image's alt text in
Shopify; there is nothing else to configure.

Renders nothing otherwise. The label is decorative (aria-hidden): the alt text
already tells screen reader users the same thing. It is not translated: "AI"
is the same in every language the theme ships.

The parent must be position: relative (the gallery frame, .media and .hero__media
are; product cards are positioned by the .product-card rule in base.css). Colors are
fixed black and white, not tokens, because the label sits on a photo and must read
on it in both color schemes. Styles are in base.css because several pages use it.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alt` | `string` | yes | The image's alt text |

```liquid
{% render 'ai-label', alt: media.alt %}
```

## breadcrumbs

File: `snippets/breadcrumbs.liquid`

Breadcrumb trail and its BreadcrumbList JSON-LD, built once from the same
data so they can never disagree. This is the ONLY place a BreadcrumbList is
emitted; do not add another.

Rules (Google and WCAG):
- The trail reflects a stable site hierarchy, not the visitor's click path.
- Product: product metafield singi.primary_collection, else the collection the
  visitor came from, else the product's first collection in Shopify's order (never
  "all" or "frontpage"), else just Home > Product. So a direct visit to a product
  still shows where it lives.
- Collection and product ancestors come from the collection metafield
  singi.parent_collection, up to three levels, and, when a collection has none,
  from where the collection sits in the breadcrumb menu (theme setting
  Navigation > Breadcrumb menu, default main-menu). Metafields win over the menu.
  Pages, blogs and the collections list use the menu the same way (they have no
  metafield); an article uses its blog's place in the menu, then the blog, then itself.
  Define both metafields with `npm run seo:metafields`.
- Absolute URLs in JSON-LD; the last JSON-LD item is the current page, which is not a link and
  is not drawn in the visible trail (the heading already says it).
- The visible trail is drawn only when there is at least one ancestor besides the
  current page. A lone current page adds nothing the heading does not, so the
  nav is omitted (the JSON-LD still lists Home and the page). Sections then get
  their normal top padding, because the breadcrumb spacing rule needs the nav.
- Home is in the JSON-LD but not in the visible trail (saves space).
- Semantic nav > ol > li, separators drawn by CSS.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `string` | yes | product, collection, collections, article, blog or page |

```liquid
{% render 'breadcrumbs', kind: 'product' %}
```

## image

File: `snippets/image.liquid`

Responsive image with the loading strategy decided in one place.

- priority: the LCP candidate. Eager, fetchpriority=high and a preload hint.
  Use for at most one image per page.
- eager: visible in the first viewport but not the LCP candidate. Eager only.
- neither: lazy and async decoded.

Width and height attributes come from image_tag, so layout never shifts.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `image` | yes | The image to render |
| `sizes` | `string` | no | The sizes attribute. Default: 100vw |
| `widths` | `string` | no | Comma separated srcset widths |
| `width` | `number` | no | Largest width to request. Default: 1600 |
| `alt` | `string` | no | Alt text. Default: the image's own alt text |
| `decorative` | `boolean` | no | Empty alt text, for a thumbnail whose product name is right next to it |
| `class` | `string` | no | Class for the img element |
| `priority` | `boolean` | no | Mark as the LCP image |
| `eager` | `boolean` | no | Load eagerly without a preload |
| `crossorigin` | `string` | no | Set to anonymous when scripts must read the pixels (assets/image-tone.js) |

```liquid
{% render 'image', image: section.settings.image, priority: true, sizes: '100vw' %}
{% render 'image', image: product.featured_image, sizes: '(min-width: 56em) 25vw, 50vw' %}
```

## localization-selector

File: `snippets/localization-selector.liquid`

Country and language selector, rendered in the footer. Hidden unless the store
has more than one country or language.

Plain markup: one `localization` form whose options are submit buttons, so it
works with no JavaScript. Choosing an option posts to Shopify, which sets the
market and returns to the current page.

Performance: `localization.available_countries` can hold about 240 countries
on a store with a "Rest of world" market. With more than 12 countries the list
is not rendered on page load. It is fetched the first time the selector is
opened, through the Section Rendering API (assets/localization.js). That is
detected with `section.index`, which is nil in Section Rendering API responses
and in the theme editor, so those always get the full list.

Must be rendered inside a section (it reads `section.id` and `section.index`).

```liquid
{% render 'localization-selector' %}
```

File: `snippets/newsletter.liquid`

## pagination

File: `snippets/pagination.liquid`

Pagination for a {% paginate %} object. Two styles:

- numbered (default): accessible page links, crawlable, no JavaScript.
- show_more: a "Show more" button that is a REAL link to the next page
  (rel="next"). Crawlers follow it, every ?page=N stays a self-canonical,
  indexable page, and without JavaScript it simply navigates. With JavaScript
  (assets/show-more.js) a normal click loads the next page's products into the
  list in place, announces "Showing N of M", moves focus to the first new
  product, and survives Back through history.state. Modified clicks (new tab)
  follow the link.

Do not add rel="nofollow" to pagination links: it hides deeper pages from
crawlers. Page N titles and self-referencing canonicals come from
snippets/meta-tags.liquid and Shopify.

The list that grows needs the attribute data-show-more-list.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paginate` | `object` | yes | The paginate object from {% paginate %} |
| `type` | `string` | no | numbered (default) or show_more |
| `page_items` | `number` | no | Items on this page (show_more) |
| `total` | `number` | no | Items in the whole result (show_more) |
| `section_id` | `string` | no | section.id of the calling section (show_more) |

```liquid
{% render 'pagination', paginate: paginate, type: 'show_more', page_items: collection.products.size, total: collection.products_count, section_id: section.id %}
```

## placeholder

File: `snippets/placeholder.liquid`

Editor-only hint for unfinished content. Renders a dashed box only while the
store is being edited or previewed: the theme editor, the editor's visual
preview, or an unpublished or development theme. In production it renders
nothing, so unfinished content can never ship to customers.

Fail-closed: if the signals are missing or change, the hint stays hidden.
`theme.role` is deprecated by Shopify, so it is only ever used to ADD preview
contexts, never to decide that something is safe to show.

The label is editor-facing English and intentionally not translated: it
never reaches a customer.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | yes | What the merchant should do here |
| `wide` | `boolean` | no | Use the tall variant for section-sized gaps |

```liquid
{% render 'placeholder', label: 'Hero: choose an image and add blocks', wide: true %}
```

## product-card

File: `snippets/product-card.liquid`

Product card. Renders its own <li>, so call it inside a <ul role="list"> and do
not wrap it. Minimal markup on purpose: this runs once per product, so every
node here is multiplied by the page size. The li is the card, the image is a
direct child (no media wrapper), the title link stretches over the card with
::after, and the badge is positioned against the li.

A product with no image shows settings.placeholder_image when the merchant set one,
otherwise an empty neutral block of the same shape, so the grid never shifts.

Why one stretched link and not a wrapper link: docs/decisions/001-stretched-card-link.md.

Only image and price are rendered inside; do not nest further snippets here.
The wishlist heart is one button, drawn with a CSS mask (no SVG), shown when the
Wishlist theme settings allow it. Its behavior lives in assets/wishlist.js.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | yes | The product to render |
| `eager` | `boolean` | no | Load the image eagerly (first row only) |
| `sizes` | `string` | no | Image sizes attribute |
| `heading` | `string` | no | Heading element for the title: h2 under a page h1, h3 under an h2 section. Default: h3 |

```liquid
<ul class="product-grid" role="list">
  {% render 'product-card', product: product, eager: true, heading: 'h2' %}
</ul>
```

## product-zoom

File: `snippets/product-zoom.liquid`

The full screen image viewer of the product page: one native <dialog>, opened by the zoom buttons that
sections/main-product.liquid puts over each gallery image. assets/zoom.js fills it. Decision record:
docs/decisions/014-product-image-zoom-is-a-native-dialog.md.

It shows the image the shopper chose, at the largest size the store has, fitted to the screen (a click
or the Zoom button shows it twice as wide, and the stage scrolls), the image's own description, and, when
the image belongs to variants, "Shown for: Moss / M". Previous and next buttons and the arrow keys move
through the images; Escape or the close button return to the gallery with focus on the button that opened it.

The image's width and height attributes are only there for the markup rules: CSS sizes the image and the loaded file brings its own ratio.

Rendered once per page, only when the setting "Let shoppers zoom product images" is on. The dialog is
modal, so the page behind it is inert. Focus starts on the Close button (autofocus), not on the scrolling stage, so no ring is drawn around the picture on open.

```liquid
{% render 'product-zoom' %}
```

## quantity-input

File: `snippets/quantity-input.liquid`

Quantity stepper: minus button, number input, plus button. Without JavaScript
it is a plain number input (the buttons stay invisible but keep their space until assets/quantity-input.js
upgrades the element). The buttons use aria-disabled at the limits so keyboard
focus is never lost, and a polite live region announces the new value.

Pair it with a <label for="{{ id }}"> (visible or visually hidden). Stepping
fires a normal `change` event, so forms and assets/cart-items.js react as if
the number had been typed.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | id of the input, for the label |
| `name` | `string` | yes | name of the input |
| `value` | `number` | yes | current quantity |
| `min` | `number` | no | lowest allowed quantity (the variant's quantity rule). Default: 1 |
| `max` | `number` | no | highest value: the rule's maximum or the stock, whichever is lower |
| `increment` | `number` | no | the quantity moves in steps of this size from the minimum (a rule). Default: 1 |
| `zero` | `boolean` | no | 0 is also allowed: the cart, where 0 removes the line |
| `hint_max` | `number` | no | the rule's own maximum, named in the hint. Stock is never named (decision 015) |
| `line` | `number` | no | cart line number: adds data-quantity and data-line for cart-items.js A hint under the control names the non-default limits ("Minimum 6 · Multiples of 6 · Maximum 24") and is the input's description. With no rule there is no hint. Decision record: docs/decisions/015-quantity-limits-follow-the-rule-and-never-name-the-stock.md. |

```liquid
{% render 'quantity-input', id: 'quantity-main', name: 'quantity', value: 1 %}
```

File: `snippets/schema-collection.liquid`

## schema-site

File: `snippets/schema-site.liquid`

Organization and WebSite structured data for the home page, as one linked
@graph. The @id values are reused by other schema snippets so the pieces
connect: `/#organization` and `/#website`.

- Organization: name, url, logo (ImageObject), sameAs from the Social profile

  hasMerchantReturnPolicy for a specific brand here, not elsewhere.

## search-results

File: `snippets/search-results.liquid`

The results under the header search field (one ARIA listbox) and their styles. Rendered by
sections/predictive-search.liquid for each request, and rendered once, empty, by the header so
these styles are on every page: the section is only ever fetched, never placed, so a
stylesheet of its own would never reach the page.

Two parts:
1. Suggestions (the search terms Shopify proposes, then matching collections) are the lower part
   of the search box: they share one border with the field, like Google's extended input.
2. Below the box: the first three matching products (so the whole list fits a phone screen
   without scrolling), pages and articles, and a "Show all for ..." button that goes to the
   full results page.

The links are the options (role="option"); the input is the combobox and points at the active
one with aria-activedescendant while focus stays in the field. They are also normal tab stops: Tab goes from
the field to the suggestions, then the products, pages and the button. data-status carries the sentence announced in a live region.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `object` | no | The predictive_search object (only available in the section, so it is passed in) |

```liquid
{% render 'search-results', results: predictive_search %}
```

## theme-init

File: `snippets/theme-init.liquid`

The theme's one inline script, rendered in the head of both layouts
(`npm run check:rules` allows no other). It does two small things that must
happen before first paint, plus one tiny handler that is not about paint:

1. Color mode. Sets it before paint (no flash) and handles the light/dark toggle.
   A saved choice in localStorage wins over the device setting and the theme's
   default color mode. The toggle button is any element with data-theme-toggle.

2. Product image placeholder. Clicking a link to a product remembers the card
   image the browser has already loaded (its exact URL, so it is in the HTTP
   cache). On the product page that URL is exposed as --placeholder, and the
   first gallery image sits on it (see sections/main-product.liquid) until the
   full-size image arrives, so the hero never flashes empty. It is only used when
   the saved path matches the page and is under 30 seconds old. window.singiPlaceholder()
   re-applies it after a soft navigation.

3. Grid or list view. A saved "list" choice (localStorage singi-view) is put on <html> as
   data-view before first paint, so a collection or search page never shows the grid and then
   jumps to the list. The radios of snippets/view-toggle.liquid follow it after load and after
   a soft navigation, and a change saves the new choice. Decision 010.

4. Search focus. When the header's search panel (a popover) opens, focus moves to its
   input. The HTML autofocus attribute is not used: it would fire on page load instead.
   (assets/predictive-search.js also focuses it inside the tap, which iOS needs for the
   keyboard; this handler covers the moment before that module has loaded.)

```liquid
{% render 'theme-init' %}
```

## unit-price

File: `snippets/unit-price.liquid`

Unit price of a variant, for comparing sizes: "$78.00 / 100 ml". Renders nothing when the
variant has no unit price set. Shopify's own filter (unit_price_with_measurement) prints
"$78.00/100ml" and cannot be spaced, so the pieces are formatted here: the price with the
store's money format, a reference value of 1 left out ("$24.00 / L", not "/ 1 L"), and unit
symbols written the usual way (L, m², ft²). Shopify returns the unit lowercase.

Screen readers get a full sentence instead of the slash (products.unit_price_per, for example
"$78.00 per 100 ml"), so each language keeps its own word order.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `variant` | yes | The variant |
| `part` | `string` | no | 'visible' for the text shown, 'label' for the screen reader sentence. Both are plain text with ordinary spaces (assets/product-form.js reads them from data attributes). Default: the finished <p> with both. |

```liquid
{% render 'unit-price', variant: product.selected_or_first_available_variant %}
```

## view-toggle

File: `snippets/view-toggle.liquid`

Grid or list view for a page of product cards, with no JavaScript: two radio chips (the same
.chip pattern as the variant picker) and a few CSS rules that react to the checked one with
:has() on the wrapper. Render it inside <div class="view-wrap">, BEFORE <facets-form>: facets.js
replaces everything inside facets-form on every filter change, so a toggle inside it would reset to
the grid each time.

The choice is remembered: snippets/theme-init.liquid saves it (localStorage singi-view), puts a saved
"list" on <html> as data-view before first paint (so there is no flash of the grid) and keeps these radios
in step. Without JavaScript the radios still work, but nothing is remembered and the grid is the default.
Decision record: docs/decisions/010-grid-and-list-view-without-javascript.md.

The toggle sits on the filter bar's line, at its end: the bar leaves room for it (padding-inline-end on
.facets) and the toggle is placed over that room. All of it is logical properties, so it mirrors in right to left.

In the list view the card's image is a fixed 7.5rem column and the text sits beside it. The card's
absolutely placed parts (AI label, favorite heart) are positioned against the image's corner, not the card's. The sold out badge moves into the text column, above the title, because the narrow image has no room for it beside the heart. The quick add button (when on) keeps the image's bottom start corner. The text is centered beside the image with two spacer rows.

```liquid
<div class="view-wrap">
  {% render 'view-toggle' %}
  <facets-form>...</facets-form>
</div>
```

## wishlist-item

File: `snippets/wishlist-item.liquid`

One saved product as a cart-style row: thumbnail, title, price and two small icon
controls. The first is exactly one of three states: a primary add to cart (the saved
variant, or the only variant, is available: adds it at once), the same button disabled
with a check once that variant is in the cart (assets/wishlist.js switches it as the cart
changes), or a secondary link with an arrow to the product page (a variant has to be
chosen, or it is sold out). The second is the pressed heart (the same secondary button as
on the product page; it removes the item). Fetched by assets/wishlist.js through
templates/product.wishlist.liquid.

Self-contained on purpose: it owns its CSS. The cart page renders this snippet
once without a product (it outputs nothing) so Shopify includes the CSS there,
because the rows themselves are inserted by JavaScript.

The saved variant arrives as ?variant=ID (product.selected_variant), so the row shows
that variant's title, price, image and stock.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product` | `product` | no | The saved product. Without one the snippet only carries its CSS. |

```liquid
{% render 'wishlist-item', product: product %}
```
